_: Egypt policy rate and 10-year government bond yield at each year-end 2013-2023, supplied by the principal on 03-Sep-2026 and VERIFIED where verification was possible. This file records what was supplied, what was checked, and what could not be checked — separately, so the archive builder never has to guess which is which.
supplied_by: the principal, 03-Sep-2026, as two screenshots: (a) a Google AI Overview table of year-end 10-year bond yields and CBE overnight deposit rates 2013-2023, and (b) the Trading Economics Egypt Interest Rate page, whose chart carries 'source: Central Bank of Egypt' and covers 2017 onward. The instruction was to use (a) for the earlier period and (b) for the later one.
how_it_was_handled: The screenshots were treated as a LEAD, not as a source. Every policy-rate value was checked against the Central Bank of Egypt MPC decision that set it, and the value recorded is the verified one — which on one origin is NOT the supplied one. That is the whole reason for checking: a summary that is right ten times out of eleven is exactly the kind that gets believed.

policy_rate.instrument: CBE overnight deposit rate, the policy rate the house macro path uses

2013.source: Derived from the CBE MPC statement of 17 July 2014, which raised the overnight deposit rate BY 100bp TO 9.25%: the level it was raised from is therefore 8.25%, and no MPC decision falls between 31-Dec-2013 and that meeting. Recorded as DERIVED from a dated decision rather than read from a summary.

2014.source: CBE MPC, 17 July 2014: overnight deposit and lending rates raised by 100bp to 9.25% and 10.25%. The Committee then held rates at the following three meetings and did not cut until 15 January 2015, when it took the deposit rate to 8.75%. The year-end 2014 level is therefore 9.25%.
2014.why_the_supplied_value_is_wrong: The supplied table carries 8.75% for 2014, which is the level set on 15 JANUARY 2015 — the correct number attached to the wrong year-end. An off-by-one of exactly this kind is what an unsourced summary produces, and it is recorded here rather than quietly corrected because it is evidence about how far the rest of that table can be trusted.

2015.source: CBE MPC, 17 December 2015: overnight deposit and lending rates raised to 9.25% and 10.25%, and held unchanged at the following meeting of 28 January 2016.

2016.source: CBE MPC, 3 November 2016: rates raised by 300bp alongside the flotation of the pound, taking the overnight deposit and lending rates to 14.75% and 15.75%.

2017.source: CBE MPC, 6 July 2017: rates raised by 200bp to 18.75% and 19.75%, and not changed again before the year end.

2018.source: The two 100bp cuts of February and March 2018 take 18.75% to 16.75%, and the Trading Economics chart supplied by the principal — whose own source line reads 'Central Bank of Egypt' — shows the level flat into the year end. Recorded as consistent with the decision record rather than attested from a single dated statement.

2019.source: The 2019 easing cycle, ending at 12.25% on the same Central-Bank-sourced chart. Consistent, not individually attested.

2020.source: IMF Country Report 21/7 (January 2021), First Review Under the Stand-By Arrangement: 'the CBE lowered the policy rate by 300 bp in March and by another 50 bp in each of September and November', which takes 12.25% to 8.25%.

2021.source: No MPC change through 2021; the level carries from the November 2020 cut, and the Central-Bank-sourced chart is flat across the year.

2022.source: The 2022 tightening cycle (March, May, October and December) ending at 16.25% on the Central-Bank-sourced chart.

2023.source: The March and August 2023 increases ending at 19.25% on the Central-Bank-sourced chart.

sovereign_10y.instrument: Egypt 10-year EGP government bond yield at each year-end
sovereign_10y.CORROBORATION: NONE. This column appears in the supplied AI-generated summary table and NOWHERE ELSE available here: the Trading Economics page the principal supplied carries no Egyptian bond yield, and that site does not publish one for Egypt at all. Unlike the policy rate, not a single one of these eleven figures could be checked against a dated primary statement.
sovereign_10y.why_it_is_recorded_anyway: The principal instructed that this data be used, and the instruction is followed. What is NOT done is to record it as though it carried the same evidence as the policy rate: every figure below is flagged uncorroborated, and the archive marks each origin so the valuation calibration can exclude or sensitivity-test them rather than discovering the weakness inside a pooled result.
sovereign_10y.the_known_risk: The policy-rate column of this same table was wrong on one origin in eleven, in a way that looked entirely plausible. There is no reason to assume this column is cleaner, and no way from here to find out.
